stale.where: HTML line 14 (opening box, 'People named here who are accused of nothing') — KNOWN DEFECT 1
current: Amber Robinson and Matthew Robinson appear only as elimination-sample donors — people whose profiles are obtained precisely so they can be identified and set aside — sought because they were associated with the premises, not as suspects. No inference about any of them may be drawn from this page.
replacement: Amber Robinson and Matthew Robinson are elimination-sample donors — people whose DNA profiles are obtained precisely so they can be identified and set aside — sought because they were associated with the premises and not as suspects. The record does contain support-for-inclusion results naming two of the three people named here: Matthew Robinson on ATF items 1.4 (the bolt) and 1.6 (the barrel), and Lance Twiggs on swabs of the buttons of the Dremel rotary tool and other areas of that tool. A “support for inclusion” statement is not a source attribution — the ATF analyst corrected counsel’s contrary phrasing three times and counsel expressly accepted the correction. Two things travel with those results: defence counsel’s framing, put in a leading question and assented to by the witness — “not because he’s a suspect, but because he’s associated with that premise” — and the analyst’s own words about household items, “it’s reasonable to assume that anyone living in the household could have contributed to DNA on an object found in that household.” No inference about any of them may be drawn from this page.
stale.note: Verbatim withdrawn form. Fifteen hits, one passage. The replacement is the docx para 8 form, which discloses both persons' results together (C-02 satisfied) and attributes the 'not as suspects' framing to defence counsel's leading question (C-04). A foot paragraph mirroring the docx's 'The living-persons note, narrowed — 1 September 2026' record is also owed. C-02's asymmetry does not arise in the live page because it discloses neither result; C-01's understatement does.
